## Problem and numerical basis

The optimization minimizes the lean-solvent flow scale $s=L/L_{3\mathrm{C}}$ at a carbon dioxide capture target of 90%.
The scale multiplies the three liquid feeds together, preserving the nominal lean loading and unloaded amine mass fraction.
The calculation uses the 6 m case 3C bed, the twelve-state conserved model, 17 cosine nodes with upwind cells, and the equilibrium-manifold film with nine quadrature points.
The calculation retains the pre-joint-fit thermodynamic parameters used in the Stage 2 reference.
The nominal liquid inlet temperature of 318.15 K was imputed, and the caloric reference remains provisional.

The [baseline](results/runs/stage0_3c_n17_base_1972203/attempt.json) captured 89.4148804% at $s=1$.
The [constrained optimum](results/runs/stage2_3c_n17_problem_p/optimum.json) was $s^*=1.024745661793$, or 2.139726 kg/s of loaded lean liquid.
The Stage 3 comparisons test numerical reproducibility on this grid and the sensitivity of this optimum to changes in the input quantities.

## Second start

IPOPT started at $s=1.15$ with the same initial nodal profile as the constrained optimum.
The [second start](results/runs/stage3_3c_n17_second_start/attempt.json) converged to $s_2^*=1.024745587820$ in 31 iterations and 597.20 s.
The scaled residual infinity norm was $6.10\times10^{-12}$, and the physical certificate accepted the profile.
The difference $|s_2^*-s^*|=7.3973\times10^{-8}$ defines $\mathrm{tol}_s$ for the sensitivity comparisons.
It measures agreement between two starts on a fixed grid.
A sample late in the second start recorded 575 s of CPU time over 583 s of elapsed time, about 98.6% of one core.
The second start required 31 iterations, compared with five for the reference solve.

## Capture around the optimum (O4)

The ordinary column solver used separate case files with each liquid feed multiplied by the indicated solvent scale.
The initial bulk state used those same liquid CO₂ and water flows.
The cases use direct SI inputs, so the transport declaration does not restrict the case paths.

| Case | Solvent scale | Capture (%) | Wall time (s) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| [1% below optimum](results/runs/stage3_3c_n17_o4_low/attempt.json) | 1.014498205 | 89.7607166 | 117.86 |
| [Optimum](results/runs/stage3_3c_n17_o4_center/attempt.json) | 1.024745662 | 90.0000019 | 130.79 |
| [1% above optimum](results/runs/stage3_3c_n17_o4_high/attempt.json) | 1.034993118 | 90.2352449 | 125.62 |

All three solves passed numerical and physical certification.
The outer cases bracketed 90% capture, and $\eta(s^*)-0.90=+1.8625\times10^{-8}$ as a fraction, within the $10^{-7}$ feasibility tolerance.
The centered difference gave $d\eta/ds=0.23153470$, compared with $1/(\lambda_c F_{V,\mathrm{CO_2,in}})=0.23150360$.
The relative slope difference was 0.0134%, and the plan specifies no separate tolerance for slope agreement.

## Sensitivity checks (O5)

Each perturbed problem used the Stage 2 nodal profile and solvent scale as its starting point.
The capture target moved by $\Delta=0.005$ in capture fraction, the lean loading by $\Delta=0.005$ mol CO₂ per mol MEA, and the liquid inlet temperature by $\Delta=1$ K.
The lean-loading perturbation changes the CO₂ feed and holds the MEA and water feeds fixed.
Each direction used four re-solves at $-2\Delta$, $-\Delta$, $+\Delta$, and $+2\Delta$.

The exact scale derivative is $-\mathrm{lam}_p$ in each input coordinate.
For lean loading, the CO₂ coordinate derivative is multiplied by the nominal MEA molar feed.
The finite-difference check accepts a direction when
$$
\left|D_{\mathrm{exact}}-D_{\mathrm{FD}}(\Delta)\right|
\leq
\max\left(
\left|D_{\mathrm{FD}}(2\Delta)-D_{\mathrm{FD}}(\Delta)\right|,
2\,\mathrm{tol}_s/\Delta
\right).
$$

| Input direction | Multiplier | FD(Δ) | FD(2Δ) | Absolute error | Allowed error | Result |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Capture target (per fraction) | 4.31958725 | 4.3197567 | 4.32016869 | 0.000169451004 | 0.000411990504 | Pass |
| Lean loading (per mol CO₂/mol MEA) | 11.5666215 | 11.5197568 | 11.3819525 | 0.0468646946 | 0.137804269 | Pass |
| Liquid inlet temperature (per K) | 0.0102853337 | 0.0102897835 | 0.0103030003 | 4.44985732e-06 | 1.32168141e-05 | Pass |

All twelve perturbed solves passed numerical and physical certification.
The capture inequality remained active to the scaled feasibility tolerance, and the state and solvent-scale bounds remained inactive.
These comparisons support the multiplier derivatives for the tested directions on this mesh.

| Input direction | −2Δ wall time (s) | −Δ (s) | +Δ (s) | +2Δ (s) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Capture target | 144.43 | 148.76 | 124.84 | 120.78 |
| Lean loading | 158.74 | 146.18 | 127.57 | 133.79 |
| Liquid inlet temperature | 150.16 | 146.84 | 136.45 | 151.69 |

## Scope and retained evidence

The comparisons verify feasibility and first-order sensitivity for the local numerical optimum on the 17-node grid.
The attempt files preserve the solver settings, the inlet basis, and physical certification.
The [summary](results/runs/stage3_3c_n17_summary.json) retains the calculated comparisons, individual perturbed optima, and wall times.
The first [low-flow attempt](results/runs/stage3_3c_n17_o4_low_interrupted/run.log) ended during a workspace routing interruption and the output recorder reported a JSON error for byte-valued worker output.
The successful retry supplied the low-flow value in the O4 table.

## Mesh dependence of the optimum

This ladder verifies the numerical solution of problem P on three cosine meshes.
The retained 17-node optimum supplies the nodal profile and solvent scale for 33 nodes, and the 33-node optimum supplies both for 65 nodes.
The solver interpolates the physical nodal states row by row.
All three calculations use nine film quadrature points and a scaled solver tolerance of $10^{-7}$.
The 33- and 65-node wall limits were 3600 s and 7200 s, respectively.

| Nodes | $s^*(N)$ | CO₂ capture (%) | $\lambda_c$ (s/mol) | Scaled NLP residual | IPOPT iterations | Wall time (s) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| [17](results/runs/stage2_3c_n17_problem_p/optimum.json) | 1.024745661793 | 90.000001713 | 2.61153181 | $1.61\times10^{-11}$ | 5 | 195.52 |
| [33](results/runs/stage5_3c_n33/attempt.json) | 1.059549737618 | 90.000000206 | 3.86727864 | $1.31\times10^{-10}$ | 8 | 341.97 |
| [65](results/runs/stage5_3c_n65/attempt.json) | 1.092517524865 | 90.000000559 | 5.43326077 | $2.16\times10^{-9}$ | 7 | 616.73 |

IPOPT reported `Solve_Succeeded` and the physical certificate accepted all three profiles.
Capture was the sole active inequality at each resolution.
Scaled capture slacks were $1.71\times10^{-8}$, $2.06\times10^{-9}$, and $5.59\times10^{-9}$, respectively.
Every state bound, including the cell states, and both solvent-scale bounds had scaled slack greater than $10^{-7}$.
The smallest scaled bound slacks were 0.05008, 0.05072, and 0.05151, respectively.

With the cosine clustering fixed, doubling the number of intervals halves the grid parameter step.
The increases in $s^*$ were 0.03480408 and 0.03296779, which give the observed order
$p_{\mathrm{obs}}=\log_2[(s^*_{33}-s^*_{17})/(s^*_{65}-s^*_{33})]=0.0781992$ under a single leading error power.
The formal Richardson limit is $s^*_{65}+(s^*_{65}-s^*_{33})/(2^{p_{\mathrm{obs}}}-1)=1.68440434$.
The extrapolation adds 0.591887 to the fine-grid optimum, almost 18 times the last observed change.
The three meshes therefore give a poorly conditioned extrapolation and leave the mesh-independent solvent requirement unresolved.

The physical capture multiplier is $\lambda_c=\mathrm{lam}_{g,c}/\sigma_c$, with $\sigma_c=1.654043516$ mol/s.
The entries below use the sign convention $\partial s^*/\partial p=-\mathrm{lam}_p$.
Each entry is per unit of its input quantity.

| Input | Unit | `lam_p` at 33 nodes | `lam_p` at 65 nodes |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Liquid CO₂ feed | mol/s | −1.79084297 | −2.50748638 |
| Liquid MEA feed | mol/s | 0.678785598 | 0.922529803 |
| Liquid water feed | mol/s | −0.0154418934 | −0.0231766181 |
| Vapour CO₂ feed | mol/s | −1.24116838 | −1.54221715 |
| Vapour water feed | mol/s | −0.135459511 | −0.150767217 |
| Vapour nitrogen feed | mol/s | 0.0426752726 | 0.0621899024 |
| Vapour oxygen feed | mol/s | 0.0427398956 | 0.0622760752 |
| Liquid inlet temperature | K | −0.0111368167 | −0.0134793120 |
| Vapour inlet temperature | K | −0.00190366996 | −0.00212967723 |
| Bottom pressure | Pa | −0.00000849526753 | −0.0000128553896 |
| Capture target | fraction | −6.39664716 | −8.98684974 |

The capture multiplier more than doubles from 17 to 65 nodes, and several inlet sensitivities also change materially.
The Stage 3 perturbations verify derivatives at fixed mesh resolution, and these changes quantify their mesh dependence for this case.

## Film quadrature and solver tolerance at 17 nodes

Both checks start from the reference optimum's solvent scale and initialize the nodal states from the feeds.
The retained-profile guard requires matching quadrature and tolerance settings, so these comparisons also change the nodal start relative to the Stage 2 reference.
The two-start scale difference on the reference settings was $7.40\times10^{-8}$.

| Change from the reference | $s^*$ | $s^*-s^*_{17}$ | CO₂ capture (%) | Scaled NLP residual | IPOPT iterations | Wall time (s) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| [9 to 17 film points](results/runs/stage5_3c_n17_film17/attempt.json) | 1.024719036748 | $-2.6625\times10^{-5}$ | 90.000000000125 | $3.09\times10^{-10}$ | 13 | 421.09 |
| [Tolerance $10^{-7}$ to $10^{-8}$](results/runs/stage5_3c_n17_tol1e8/attempt.json) | 1.024745587819 | $-7.3974\times10^{-8}$ | 90.000000000216 | $1.30\times10^{-12}$ | 13 | 237.01 |

Both calculations used 3600 s wall limits and returned certified profiles with capture active and all bounds inactive.
The quadrature shift is about three orders of magnitude smaller than the 17-to-33-node shift.
The tighter-tolerance optimum agrees with the second-start optimum to within $10^{-12}$ in $s$.
Linear solvers for the new mesh, quadrature and tolerance runs are unknown from their retained records.

The first launches of [33 nodes](results/runs/stage5_3c_n33_preflight/run.log), [17 film points](results/runs/stage5_3c_n17_film17_preflight/run.log), and the [tighter tolerance](results/runs/stage5_3c_n17_tol1e8_preflight/run.log) stopped during configuration validation.
The modified requests retained the original configuration checksum, so no column worker started.
The reruns resolved the modified requests from the original input file and supplied the results above.

## Engine work with exact and forward-difference Jacobians

This numerical comparison holds the constrained NLP, inlet values, initial scale and retained stage 0 nodal seed, solver options and solver tolerance fixed within each mesh pair.
The changed calculation is the Jacobian of each Engine callback.
It uses a forward perturbation $h_j=r u_j$ on one positive Engine input $u_j$ at a time.
The residual still consumes Engine first actions for the loading tangent and caloric slopes in both arms.
The comparison therefore measures the cost of approximating the callback Jacobians for this residual.

The [step sweep](results/runs/stage4_3c_n17_step_sweep/attempt.json) evaluated the scaled constraint Jacobian with respect to the NLP decision variables at a converged 17-node optimum.
The error was the largest entrywise error in each column divided by the greater of 1 and the largest exact entry magnitude in that column, maximized over columns.

| Relative step $r$ | Largest scaled column error |
|---:|---:|
| $10^{-3}$ | $1.09133\times10^{-3}$ |
| $10^{-4}$ | $1.09233\times10^{-4}$ |
| $10^{-5}$ | $1.09242\times10^{-5}$ |
| $10^{-6}$ | $1.09211\times10^{-6}$ |
| $10^{-7}$ | $1.27045\times10^{-6}$ |
| $10^{-8}$ | $3.29641\times10^{-5}$ |
| $10^{-9}$ | $2.77128\times10^{-4}$ |

The comparison uses $r=10^{-6}$, which minimized the error among the tested steps.
The sweep retained the exact solve and derivative evaluations in one attempt.
Its worker elapsed time of 293.94 s includes both operations.

The primary cost is the sum of the liquid and vapour Engine `native_solves` counters.
The action-request counts include value requests sent through the same Engine action interface.
The sum of cache hits and misses counts every call to the phase equilibrium cache, including hits.
For the runs with no failed calls or continuations, cache misses minus final cache occupancy counts the evictions from each 4096-entry cache.
All counters span the worker through profile certification and include IPOPT's post-solve `lam_p` evaluation.

| Nodes | Callback Jacobian | Iterations | Primal inf. | Dual inf. | Bound violation | Engine solves | Action requests | Cache calls | Evictions |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 9 | [Exact](results/runs/stage4_3c_n9_exact_counts/attempt.json) | 13 | $6.57\times10^{-11}$ | $1.41\times10^{-8}$ | 0 | 2,344 | 87,105 | 87,105 | 0 |
| 9 | [Forward difference](results/runs/stage4_3c_n9_fd_counts/attempt.json) | 14 | $2.10\times10^{-12}$ | $9.94\times10^{-8}$ | 0 | 14,706 | 102,677 | 102,677 | 9,763 |
| 17 | [Exact](results/runs/stage4_3c_n17_exact_counts/attempt.json) | 5 | $1.61\times10^{-11}$ | $1.10\times10^{-11}$ | 0 | 1,968 | 83,841 | 83,841 | 0 |
| 17 | [Forward difference](results/runs/stage4_3c_n17_fd_counts/attempt.json) | 5 | $8.10\times10^{-11}$ | $2.15\times10^{-9}$ | 0 | 11,460 | 93,081 | 93,081 | 6,685 |

All four runs returned `Solve_Succeeded` and passed numerical and physical certification.
The absolute differences in the solvent-scale optima were $3.668\times10^{-9}$ at 9 nodes and $1.155\times10^{-12}$ at 17 nodes.
The forward differences used 6.27 and 5.82 times as many Engine equilibrium solves, respectively.
These are solver-work comparisons for case 3C on two meshes.

The retained IPOPT logs identify MUMPS 5.4.1 for the outer optimization.
The last Engine equilibrium results in the liquid and vapour phases both record MA57.

### Timing conditions

The comparison ran with single-threaded BLAS and a 3600 s worker limit per run.
Load averages at the start of the four count runs were recorded over 1, 5 and 15 minutes.

| Nodes | Exact load average | Forward-difference load average |
|---|---|---|
| 9 | 4.69 / 4.06 / 5.95 | 5.08 / 4.55 / 5.90 |
| 17 | 10.39 / 6.85 / 6.47 | 6.43 / 6.86 / 6.54 |

The first [timing repeat](results/runs/stage4_3c_n9_exact_r1/run.log) started at load averages of 2.17 / 3.70 / 5.22, with no other column process detected.
A #16 column campaign started during that solve, so its wall time is excluded.
The waiting window closed with other column activity still present.
The three uncontended repeats per configuration remain pending.
No column solve exceeded its wall limit.
